band12_scope: Do not transfer the legacy band-12 zero-fraction observation to GP. The retained independent GP pfrac result reports nonzero GP fractions in upper layers while saved GP GAS_TAU_RAW is zero there; the older legacy fraction record has its own zero-fraction upper-layer behavior. These are distinct table/engine facts. This design will reconstruct GP major/minor absorption from its own coefficients and inputs; it will not infer zero GP tau from pfrac alone, normalize fractions, or use legacy fraction masks as GP masks. No band-12 opacity values were computed here.

coefficient_inventory.major_table_internal_order: NetCDF exposes kmajor dimensions (temperature,pressure_interp,mixing_fraction,gpt). The Fortran loader reads it with requested extents (ngpt,nmix,npress+1,ntemps), then init_abs_coeffs reshapes to this%kmajor dimensions (temperature,eta,pressure_interp,gpt) using ORDER=(/4,2,3,1/) (frontend:1390-1396). This final internal layout matches the kernel dummy declaration (ntemp,neta,npres+1,ngpt; kernels:222). A Python reader must use NetCDF dimension names; a Fortran-order translation must reproduce both read_field and reshape order.

minor_filtering.full_row_map: See the separately pinned minor-metadata-inventory-v1.json for each interval's identifier, mapped absorber, active status, inclusive g-point bounds, original and filtered kminor_start, density/complement flags, and scaling gas.
minor_filtering.rule: For every minor_gases_lower/upper entry, map identifier_minor -> gas_minor to get absorber name; retain when absorber is in host available_gases (frontend reduce_minor_arrays). Coefficient file gas_minor/identifier_minor are not the same strings as every minor_gases interval entry (e.g. h2o_frgn/h2o_self map to h2o).

coefficient_inventory.minor_table_internal_order: NetCDF kminor dimensions are (temperature,mixing_fraction,contributors). The Fortran loader reads kminor_lower/upper using extents (ncontributors,nmixingfracs,ntemps) (mo_load_coefficients.F90:134-137). The frontend filters and repacks each contributor interval and reshapes the compact table; the kernel receives (ntemp,neta,nminork) (mo_gas_optics_rrtmgp_kernels.F90:427). Python should bind fields by NetCDF dimension names, while any Fortran-equivalent translated representation must follow this read/repack/reshape mapping rather than treating flattened contributor positions as g-point IDs. Exact interval metadata and retained starts are in minor-metadata-inventory-v1.json.
coefficient_inventory.unit_attributes: The coefficient variables inspected in this NetCDF do not carry units attributes. Use the code's documented column-amount units and formulas; do not infer units solely from array magnitudes or add guessed scale factors.

feasibility_and_traps.component_scope: The saved opacity result exposes the combined absorption total but not major, minor, or per-species partial arrays, nor interpolation indices/weights. A complete independent translation can compute those components, but the stored target only checks their final ordered sum; separate component validation would need an additional observer.
feasibility_and_traps.feasible: A direct independent Python implementation is feasible from the held input, saved N2 argv, pinned coefficient file, and source. It is not a short k-major multiply: reproduce gas-name reduction, flavor maps, contributor filtering/offset correction, pressure regime windows, and density/special-gas rules. For this exact LW file, no Rayleigh term needs to be synthesized or subtracted.
feasibility_and_traps.interpretation: A successful calculation would validate a source-translated opacity implementation against the pinned GP result. It would not establish spectroscopic truth, RRTMG4 equivalence, or radiation accuracy. Handle GP band-12 upper layers from the pinned GP coefficients and fractions themselves; legacy zero-fraction masks are not transferable.
feasibility_and_traps.not_an_oracle_for: The pinned LW file has no Rayleigh variables/dimensions, so this call's saved GAS_TAU_RAW is the absorption-only major-plus-minor total and can be directly compared to that sum. The saved result still has no component split by major gas, minor contributor, or gas species. Other coefficient files/phases can activate the generic Rayleigh branch.

Read named variables/dimensions from the pinned LW NetCDF. Build host gas names exactly from module_ra_rrtmgp.F; map vmr_ref and key_species by species names. Apply the sole (0,0)->(2,2) rewrite and preserve table/Fortran 1-based index semantics.

Rebuild the lower/upper minor interval maps from gas_minor, identifier_minor, minor_gases_lower/upper and available_gases. Retain exact table order, per-interval g-point bounds, coefficient start-offset subtraction, density/complement/scaling-gas flags, and coefficient axis order. Compare that generated metadata map to the pinned minor-metadata-inventory-v1.json before any opacity arithmetic.

Reconstruct col_dry from the saved matched 45-row mass input using the adapter formula, then col_gas(0)=col_dry and each species column amount=VMR*col_dry. Preserve adapter REAL conversion and play/plev unit conversion.

Translate interpolation state once from source to obtain jtemp,jpress,jeta,tropo,fmajor,fminor,col_mix. Then calculate major tau, lower-minor tau and upper-minor tau in source accumulation order. Keep partial components for diagnostics, but do not treat them as separately stored oracle values.

For this pinned LW table, sum major+minor only and compare shape (1,45,128) to saved GAS_TAU_RAW. This file has no Rayleigh variables; do not add or subtract a Rayleigh term. Keep band 12 and upper-extension layers explicitly indexed; do not transfer legacy fracs masks or normalize GP fractions.
purpose: Specify a source-faithful independent reconstruction of LW gas absorption optical depth for the pinned matched-dry 45-layer BON diagnostic column. This is an implementation cross-check, not an accuracy test or transport validation.
rayleigh_and_saved_field: For this exact pinned LW coefficient file, Rayleigh is absent: its NetCDF variables and dimensions whose names contain 'rayl' are both empty. The frontend only allocates this%krayl when rayl_lower is allocated (init_abs_coeffs around 1402-1416); compute_gas_taus branches on allocated(this%krayl) at 672 and otherwise calls compute_tau_absorption directly into optical_props%tau at 720-749. Thus the actual BON LW atmos%tau and saved GAS_TAU_RAW are absorption-only for this coefficient file. The generic allocated-Rayleigh branch computes absorption and Rayleigh separately then combines them, but it is not active in this pinned call.

rayleigh_specific_correction.comparison_implication: For this coefficient file and LW call, GAS_TAU_RAW is absorption-only and the independently reconstructed ordered major+minor total is the appropriate direct comparison. This does not generalize to other data files or phases.

source_algorithm.frontend_reduction_and_flavor: Frontend init (1299-1328) intersects coefficient gas_names with host available_gases, packs runtime gas_names in coefficient table order, and remaps vmr_ref by name. It reduces key_species by species names and rejects missing key gases, builds unique flavors, then maps each g-point to flavor by its band (1445-1454). The only key-pair rewrite is (0,0)->(2,2), documented as safe because those g-points have zero absorption coefficients (1739-1747). Minor identifiers separately map identifier_minor -> gas_minor -> runtime gas indices (1808-1828). Do not assume raw coefficient absorber indices, runtime gas indices, and minor interval identifiers are interchangeable.
source_algorithm.gas_setup: Adapter module_ra_rrtmgp.F:69-75 defines ordered names_lw and fixed dry-background N2. set_gases_lw:473-512 sets the six standard gases, N2, and all-or-none four-CFC group; gas_dry_column:583-595 constructs dry columns; LW call:800-806 supplies pressure, temperature, gases and col_dry.
source_algorithm.major_absorption: compute_tau_absorption first calls gas_optical_depths_major (kernels:292-302), looping band then layer. It selects iflav=gpoint_flavor(itropo,band_lims_gpt(1,band)); interpolate3D_byflav weights the four eta/pressure corners for each of two temperature planes, multiplies by the corresponding col_mix value, and adds each band's g-point range to tau (350-401; interpolation kernel 763-790). Keep runtime kmajor order (temperature,eta,pressure_interp,gpt), with the coefficient loader read/reshape contract documented in coefficient_inventory.
source_algorithm.minor_absorption: compute_tau_absorption zeroes tau, adds major absorption first, then invokes lower and upper minor-gas passes (kernels:276-342). Each interval identifier in minor_gases_lower/upper maps through identifier_minor to gas_minor; the resulting absorber is kept only if present in available_gases. After filtering, the frontend compacts flattened coefficient segments and subtracts lengths of preceding removed g-point intervals from each retained kminor_start (frontend:1971-2088). For an active interval/layer, scaling starts at col_gas(idx_minor); if minor_scales_with_density, multiply by (0.01*play/tlay). If idx_minor_scaling>0, form vmr_fact=1/col_gas(0), dry_fact=1/(1+col_gas(idx_h2o)*vmr_fact), then multiply by either the scaling gas dry VMR or its complement according to scale_by_complement (kernels:407-503). The selected compact kminor segment is interpolated over eta and temperature using fminor/jeta/jtemp and added only to that interval's inclusive g-point range. Preserve lower/upper pressure-region layer limits, not just a per-layer major-flavor selector.
source_algorithm.minor_lower_upper_and_scaling: The frontend filters lower/upper minor interval rows separately by absorber presence and compacts contributor coefficients while shifting starts for excluded intervals (frontend:1971-2088). Runtime kernel forms layer limits for lower and upper atmosphere (kernels:276-290), then calls minor calculation twice with respective lower/upper metadata (304-342). For each interval, only its g-point limits are changed. Base scaling is the absorber column amount; optional density scaling is times 0.01*play/tlay. If a named scaling gas index is present, dry_fact uses col_gas(0) and h2o column amount; the rule multiplies by special gas dry VMR or complement. Then kminor is interpolated along eta/temp from compact table index kminor_start..start+(gptE-gptS) and added to the same selected tau g-points (407-503). H2O foreign/self identifiers both map to h2o; their own density/scaling/complement flags must be retained, not treated as distinct host VMR species.
source_algorithm.rayleigh_and_saved_field: For this pinned LW coefficient file, Rayleigh is absent. The NetCDF loader conditionally reads rayl_lower/rayl_upper only when rayl_lower exists (mo_load_coefficients.F90:165-168); this file has neither Rayleigh variables nor Rayleigh-named dimensions. init_abs_coeffs allocates this%krayl only if rayl_lower is allocated (mo_gas_optics_rrtmgp.F90:1402-1416), so compute_gas_taus follows the no-Rayleigh branch (672-750) and compute_tau_absorption writes directly into optical_props%tau. Adapter GAS_TAU_RAW is traced from atmos%tau (module_ra_rrtmgp.F:807-812). Thus the pinned saved LW GAS_TAU_RAW equals the major-plus-minor absorption result, subject to exact source ordering/precision. This is specific to the pinned LW coefficient file, not the generic frontend or other phases/files.
source_algorithm.state_interpolation: compute_gas_taus (560-671) fetches VMRs by runtime gas name, uses adapter-provided col_dry, sets col_gas(0)=col_dry and col_gas(g)=VMR(g)*col_dry, then computes interpolation state. Kernel interpolation (40-177) produces jtemp/ftemp, jpress/fpress, tropo, per-flavor/per-temperature eta, jeta/feta, col_mix, fmajor/fminor. Preserve index clipping/truncation, runtime flavor order, and source expression order. The same computed arrays feed major and minor optical-depth calculations; this task does not recompute pfrac.
